diff --git a/slugify/slugify.py b/slugify/slugify.py
--- a/slugify/slugify.py

rationale: In slugify/slugify.py:21, DUPLICATE_DASH_PATTERN was inadvertently changed to match 3 or more dashes instead of 2 or more dashes (-{2,}). patch:
diff --git a/src/cachetools/_cached.py b/src/cachetools/_cached.py
--- a/src/cachetools/_cached.py
+++ b/src/cachetools/_cached.py
@@ -261,9 +261,16 @@
             wrapper = _unlocked(func, cache, key)
         wrapper.cache_info = None
 
+    cache_clear = wrapper.cache_clear
+    cache_info = wrapper.cache_info
+
+    functools.update_wrapper(wrapper, func)
+
+    wrapper.cache_clear = cache_clear
+    wrapper.cache_info = cache_info
     wrapper.cache = cache
     wrapper.cache_key = key
     wrapper.cache_lock = lock if lock is not None else cond
     wrapper.cache_condition = cond
 
-    return functools.update_wrapper(wrapper, func)
+    return wrapper
rationale:
In `src/cachetools/_cached.py:264-269`, calling `functools.update_wrapper(wrapper, func)` at the end of `_wrapper` copies `func.__dict__` into `wrapper.__dict__`. When decorators are stacked (`func` is another wrapped function), this overwrote `wrapper`'s `cache`, `cache_clear`, `cache_info`, etc. with those of the inner wrapper.

Calling `functools.update_wrapper(wrapper, func)` before binding `wrapper`'s own attributes (`cache_clear`, `cache_info`, `cache`, `cache_key`, `cache_lock`, `cache_condition`) ensures that `wrapper` retains its own cache management attributes rather than inheriting `func.__dict__` entries.
